$comment: P127 B2 cross-runtime types-core parity fixture: object and boxing, Type and typeof, int32 wraparound and checked, explicit conversions, casts, as and default. Each case calls a static Probe function of `source` on a fresh session; `returns` pins its result and `refuses` the error message it throws. Expected values match .NET 10 except where the spec makes NeoScript differ (string box identity, NeoScript type spelling). The web half runs through `neo test` (cli/src/commands/p127-types-parity.test.ts); the Unity half runs the same cases over a `neo export`. Vendor this file verbatim. B5 fix round 1 (R19): InvalidCast messages name CLR types (.NET 10); a user type keeps its NeoScript name. R20: an explicit unbox to int or an enum accepts an int or enum box (shared underlying type); a Nullable target, is, as and IsInstanceOfType stay exact (.NET 10). UnboxUndeclaredToEnum keeps NeoScript's undeclared-option refusal (.NET gives 7). CtorBodyCatMapShared and CtorBodyIntSetShared pin main's answer, where a field a constructor body stores its collection argument in shares it with the caller, pending the follow-up on the writable-context spec's §7 copy rule. R23: the Om_<position>_<held> cases sweep `object` slots: each held value (boxes, classes, generic and derived classes, a two-level holder, collections, an `object`-closed generic) in each position (field default, required and nullable fields, static, list entry, dictionary value, a generic closed to object, constructor arguments, initializer block, run-time assignment), against the same value in a typed slot (TY, IT). Each reads, mutates and reads back; `persists` reads the written value in the next execution. The Temp column holds a temporary's member (`new OmW2(4).P`): a static's initializer takes it as its typed slot does, and an initializer block or run-time assignment refuses it in typed and `object` slots alike. FD_Temp and FN_Temp are absent (an unrelated field-default arity failure, also on main), as are GC_Temp, CA_Temp and CP_Temp, which refuse at load (static-symbol-defaults.test.ts). The Om_SC cases take a static's constructed child (`ScSrc.W.P`) in a generic class's static, which initializes at its first read: a class, `object`, `List<object>` or `Dictionary<string, object>` static refuses it as already owned, so the type initializer throws, and a Clone() initializes and reads; a run-time assignment of a whole static's value to another static refuses it as already owned, and its Clone() reads. A generic static takes a temporary's member as a non-generic static does (Om_SC_Temp*, in a typed, `List`, `Dictionary` and `object`-entry static), and a typed class-entry collection runs each computed entry per construction (Om_SC_Ctor*). The Om_SC_H cases reach another generic static's child through a function: of another construction, initialized before or during the read (HwS, HwU), or of a sibling field (HiS, HiM); each refuses as already owned, as a non-generic sibling refuses at load, and a Clone() reads (HcM). The GS column holds each value in a generic class's `object` static, which initializes at its first read, and reads as ST does. Its persists rows carry each construction's Session state into the next execution, as ST's carry a Session static's binding. The SV rows hold a Save generic static, which a save and its reload keep for each construction; SVN is the non-generic control. The OL column holds each value in a list inside an `object` list. The UL column holds each class value, and an int, in an unordered `object` list with another class entry and a scalar, and finds it by kind rather than by position. CL, CD, CS, CG and CN hold a scalar constructor argument in a collection default, CN in a nested list. A class argument there is refused at load as already owned, as in a typed slot, and a collection argument as a shared boxed collection (OwnedCollectionBoxConstructor). R28: the Rr cases hold a generic instance in a field typed by its own class's parameter (`RrPen<object>` holding `RrPen<int>`), which keeps its own type arguments for `is` and casts. R30: the RrDerived cases hold a derived generic class (`RrSubP<int> : RrPen<T>`) there, and in an `object` static, which reads its base's `T` from its own type arguments.
